accounting.rationale: The paragraph combines the constant/variable/constant-subobject partition with explicit and implicit typing of named data objects.
Data objects are constants, variables, or subobjects of constants. 9.2 and 9.3 own variable and constant usage restrictions; this does not invent a new classifier fixture.
Named data object type and type parameters can be specified explicitly or implicitly. 8.2 and 8.7 own declaration and implicit mapping constraints.

Defines subobjects as independently referenceable and, for variables, independently definable portions of data objects. Object-designator syntax and definition-status effects remain with Clauses 9 and 19.
The paragraph lists subobject families, states that subobjects are data objects, restricts reference forms, preserves variable-subobject status, and names Clause 9 as detailed owner.
Array elements/sections, substrings, complex parts, and structure components are detailed in 9.4 and 9.5. Their syntax, value, shape, and designator restrictions are not duplicated here.
Subobjects are themselves data objects; downstream owners decide whether a particular subobject is a variable, constant, definable, or referenceable in context.
Subobjects are referenced only by object designators or intrinsic functions. Designator grammar is owned by 9.1 and intrinsic-function result rules by Clause 16.
A subobject of a variable is a variable, subject to 9.2 reference/definition restrictions and the relevant designator catalogues.
Explicit cross-reference: Clause 9 owns the detailed subobject catalogues.
Lists named scalar and named array objects as objects referenced by a name. 9.2 variable-name and 8.5.8 named-array declaration rules own the detailed source plans.

Lists the subobjects referenced by object designators. The corresponding designator, substring, complex-part, structure-component, and array element/section catalogues in Clause 9 own syntax and value effects.

review_rationale: Source registration for 5.4 and 5.4.1-5.4.6 of the Clause 5 overview: type, data value, data entity, data object, definition of objects and pointers, reference and array (batch249). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; overview definitions are cross-referenced to specific owning facets in Clauses 7-19. Source accounting only.
